synopsis: The corpus treats missed hazards and false positives as a coupled calibration problem: reducing misses increases false alarms, and achieving an acceptable balance in the manufacturer's proximity-awareness system took years [f11305, f10]. Automatic braking makes false positives machine-motion hazards, with potential loss of control or conflict with following plant, while mining reports associate nuisance interventions with production losses, wear and resistance to adoption [f3024, f6303, f5567]. Acceptance planning should measure scenario-conditioned detection and intervention, dangerous misses, false warnings and unnecessary interventions per operating hour, and collision avoidance; however, no acceptance value for detection probability or miss rate was found, nor a source-attributable consensus on the acceptable miss–nuisance trade-off [f2632, f2620, f2884]. With zero misses, demonstrating miss rates of at most 1%, 0.1% and 0.01% at 95% one-sided confidence requires respectively 299, 2,995 and 29,956 independent trials per claimed population; at 99% confidence, the corresponding counts are 459, 4,603 and 46,050 [f6650, f6651, f6652, f6653]. Validation must avoid circular detector-derived ground truth and replay that assumes perception succeeded, and should retain physical ISO 21815-1 clause 6 performance and false-positive tests [f5359, f5259, f7884]. Evidence remains incomplete: NIOSH's 2022 review identified false-positive testing and other validation gaps, and published complete off-road automatic-braking false-positive and false-negative rates under adverse environmental conditions were not found [f10425, f6385].
